newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor stock seen rising on cement demand.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor stock seen rising on cement demand.

text.p: Shares in Portuguese cement company Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal could rise by between five and 10 percent before the end of the year due to strong demand for cement in the second half, analysts said.
"The nine-month results were impressive and everyone knows that it is a great time for cement," said one analyst who declined to give his name.
He forecast Cimpor would make a 1996 consolidated net profit of 18 billion escudos, excluding gains from the sale of a 12 percent stake it held in newly privatised Banco do Fomento e Exterior (BFE).
Last year Cimpor posted consolidated net of 18.4 billion escudos, down from 25.2 billion the previous year.
"Cimpor's shares could go up by between five and 10 percent by the end of the year. The operating margin looks very good," said another share analyst.

Cimpor announced on Thursday it had increased nine-month consolidated net by 40 percent from the same period in 1995 to 20.6 billion escudos. It said the revaluation of its BFE stake had had a positive impact on its result.
By 1230 GMT its shares had edged down 6 escudos to 3,268 on profit-taking after earlier reaching a high of 3,275.
"After the nine-month results I'm revising my EPS (earnings per share) estimates upward," the second analyst said.
"In the last three months the stock has under-performed and it is now a good buy," he added.
Analysts said cement consumption would probably be stronger than previously forecast in 1997.
Cimpor said in a statement that increased demand for cement in the third quarter had enabled it to raise nine-month accumulated sales by 1.6 percent over the same period last year.
But some analysts said they were perplexed by a fall in operating profit over the first nine months to 21.8 billion escudos from a previous 24.3 billion.
"I can't understand this fall given that cement sales have risen," said a third analyst.
A Cimpor spokesman told Reuters that the operating result was not directly comparable since the 1995 figure had not included various costs because of a delay in receiving invoices.
"This (third) quarter has already shown an improvement in the operating margin to around the levels of late last year," he said.
